conflicts.fact: Numbering and content of the cumulative cell model versions
conflicts.versions: L1: Version 0 is the first drawing, compared with Version 4 in Lesson 11. L2: Version 1 is a generalised eukaryotic cell, to be revised by Lesson 12. L3: adds a 'Version 2' prokaryote vs eukaryote panel. L4: Version 2 is the Plant Cell, and the existing model is called Version 1 'Animal Cell, revised in Lesson 3'. L5: Version 3 is plant vs animal side by side, with Version 2 as plant only. L10: Version 4 is the hierarchy. L7 and L8 call it a 'Cell Structure Model' or 'Cell Specialisation Model' with no version number.

conflicts.fact: When the cumulative model began and which lesson it was started in
conflicts.versions: L2 and L6: begun in Lesson 1 / Lesson 2. L7: 'running diagram updated in every lesson since Lesson 5'. L8: begun in Lesson 1. L9: Cell Specialisation Model begun in Lesson 4. L5: journal begun in Lesson 2.
L6: low power ×40, high power ×100 or ×400. L7: low ×4 objective, medium ×10, high ×40 objective.

conflicts.fact: Whether ribosomes are membrane-bound and wording about shared organelles
conflicts.versions: L3 says ribosomes are 'not membrane-bound in either' type; L2 says ribosomes are in both. These are consistent, but L2's colour code 'GREEN = both' vs L5 'black = shared' differs in wording only. No substantive conflict.

conflicts.fact: Name of the student whose finger is cut
conflicts.versions: L1, L2, L3, L5: Amina. L4: 'Kioni's cut'. L1/L6/L8/L10/L11/L12 refer to an unnamed Form 1 student, and L10 uses a Form 2 student in a school analogy.

conflicts.fact: Location of the dry vs humid guard cell comparison
conflicts.versions: L9 Overview says 'dry Turkana vs humid Kisumu' while the Observed and Explain sections say 'humid Kericho'.

L1 says 'over the next eleven lessons' (implying 12 total, consistent); L8 says 'Lesson 8 of 12'; L2 says the model runs 'by Lesson 12', while L1 says Version 4 will be compared in Lesson 11 and L12 compares with the Lesson 11 model. No substantive conflict.

conflicts.fact: Which cells are involved in wound healing
conflicts.versions: L8 says the five healing cells are red blood cells, white blood cells, nerve cells, sperm cells and muscle cells, though sperm cells do not take part in healing. L1, L10 and L12 list platelets, neutrophils, macrophages, fibroblasts and epidermal cells.

conflicts.fact: Why chloroplasts are absent / presence in guard cells and root hair
conflicts.versions: L6: chloroplasts absent from onion because the bulb is underground, with 'only in cells exposed to light'. L9: guard cells contain chloroplasts, and the root hair cell has none. Compatible; no conflict.
